# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 43 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 43 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_043_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

This chapter continues Mandate 11 with a more elaborate portrait of both prophets. The false prophet is characterized above all by two traits: desire for prominence (the "first seat") and charging money for prophecy. The latter was a standard criticism of itinerant charismatics; the Didache (11:6) similarly condemns any prophet who asks for money.

The true prophet's key characteristic is passivity — he does not speak of himself, but only when the Spirit impels him. This is a high pneumatological claim: genuine prophecy is involuntary. The phrase "the Holy Spirit of God himself rests upon this man" (*epanapauetai ep' auton to pneuma to hagion*) uses the same verb as Isaiah 11:2 LXX ("the Spirit of God shall rest upon him").

EMET's treatment of 43:7 becomes repetitive ("test the man...test him in life...see whether the life") because it preserves Hermas's doubled exhortation. LOGOS adds "virtuous" to "upright" in the final phrase; SOPHIA does not, following EMET.

---

## Mandate 11, Part 2 — Signs of the True and False Prophet

**43:1** "Hear now both the spirit of the divine and the spirit of earthly origin, and discern each by his works. Trust the spirit that comes from above, from the power of God; but the earthly spirit has no power, is empty, and is foolish."

**43:2** "First, concerning the man who seems to have the Spirit: he who exalts himself and seeks the seat of honor and is bold and shameless and loquacious and lives in luxury and in many other deceptions — and who accepts payment for his prophesying, and if he does not receive it will not prophesy — can the Spirit of God receive payment for prophesying? It is impossible for a prophet of God to do this. The spirit of such prophets, therefore, is earthly."

**43:3** "On the other hand, observe the character of the man who has the divine Spirit. The man who has the Spirit from above is gentle and quiet and humble and keeps himself from all wickedness and the empty desire of this age, and makes himself more lowly than all men, and does not respond when questioned, and does not speak of himself alone — for the Holy Spirit does not speak when a man wishes to speak, but speaks at the time when God wills him to speak."

**43:4** "When therefore the man who has the divine Spirit comes into an assembly of righteous men who have faith in the Holy Spirit, and prayer is made, the man is filled with the Holy Spirit and speaks to the congregation as God wills. In this way the Spirit of God will be made manifest. Such is the power of the Spirit of the Lord."

**43:5** "Hear now also concerning the earthly and empty spirit, which has no power but is foolish. First, that man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself and seeks the first place, and is bold and shameless and loquacious and accustomed to luxury and many other deceits, and accepts payment for his divination. When you see such a man, keep away from him."

**43:6** "Now hear again concerning the true prophet. The man who has the divine Spirit does not exalt himself or desire to speak first, nor does he live in luxury, nor does he seek payment for inquiry — but rather, if anyone inquires of him, he does not answer of himself but only by the will of God. And since the Holy Spirit of God himself rests upon this man, he speaks the things that the Lord commands."

**43:7** "When therefore both spirits come together in the same place, and you wish — through prayer for discernment — to test which is true and which is false: test the man who has the divine Spirit through his way of life. See whether the life of the man who has the spirit is consistent with upright living."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
